"'''Nice & Slow'''" is a song from American singer [[Usher (musician)|Usher]]'s second album, ''[[My Way (Usher album)|My Way]]'' (1997). Released on January 6, 1998, by [[LaFace Records|LaFace]] and [[Arista Records|Arista]], the song became Usher's first number-one single on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart in February 1998. The song was written by Usher, Brian Casey of the R&B group [[Jagged Edge (American group)|Jagged Edge]], Manuel Seal, and [[Jermaine Dupri]].

"Nice & Slow" is a song from American singer Usher's second album, My Way (1997). Released on January 6, 1998, by LaFace and Arista, the song became Usher's first number-one single on the US Billboard Hot 100 chart in February 1998. The song was written by Usher, Brian Casey of the R&B group Jagged Edge, Manuel Seal, and Jermaine Dupri.

sections.heading: Background and composition
sections.wikitext:
"Nice & Slow" was written by [[Usher (musician)|Usher]], [[Jermaine Dupri]], [[Manuel Seal]], and Brian Casey, with Dupri producing the tune and Seal serving as co-producer and responsible for the guitar work. [[Jagged Edge (American group)|Jagged Edge]] provided [[background vocals]] in the record. "Nice & Slow" was recorded by [[Phil Tan]] at the Somewhere in College Park studio in [[College Park, Georgia]]. Tan and Dupri [[audio mixing (recorded music)|mixed]] the record with assistance from John and Brian Frye at Studio LaCoCo, in [[Atlanta|Atlanta, Georgia]].<ref name="MyWay">{{cite AV media notes |title=[[My Way (Usher album)|My Way]] |year=1997 |type=CD liner |publisher=[[LaFace Records]]}}</ref> Dupri recalled telling Usher he needed a [[ballad]] to "knock out the world". The [[beat (music)|beat]] was created first, and the lyrics were fitted to it. The composition and recording of "Nice & Slow" took four hours, according to Dupri.<ref name="Bronson">{{cite book |title=The Billboard Book of Number 1 Hits |first=Fred |last=Bronson |author-link=Fred Bronson |edition=5th |year=2003 |publisher=Billboard Books ([[Watson-Guptill]]) |location=New York, NY |page=863 |isbn=0-8230-7677-6}}</ref>

"Nice & Slow" is a slow [[contemporary R&B|R&B]] and [[soul music|soul]] [[ballad]] with [[hip hop music|hip hop]] influences.<ref name="sheet"/><ref name="romance"/><ref>{{cite book|title=The Virgin Encyclopedia of R&B and Soul |first=Colin |last=Larkin |publisher=[[Virgin Publishing]] |date=August 1998 |isbn=9780753502419 |page=342}}</ref> Musicologist Richard J. Ripani wrote that "Nice & Slow" is an example of the typical "R&B ballad style that became widely popular" in the late 1990s.<ref>{{cite book |title=The New Blue Music: Changes in Rhythm & Blues, 1950-1999 |first=Richard J. |last=Ripani |chapter=Rap Goes Mainstream: 1990–1999 |page=156 |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fFno4HDB7uYC&pg=PA156%22 |date=July 27, 2006 |publisher=[[University Press of Mississippi]] |location=[[Jackson, Mississippi]] |isbn=9781578068616}}</ref> According to the sheet music published at Musicnotes.com by [[Universal Music Publishing Group]], "Nice & Slow" is written in common time with a slow [[tempo]] of sixty-eight beats per minute. Set in the [[key (music)|key]] of [[A-flat major|A{{music|flat}} major]], it follows the basic [[chord progression]] of Fm<sub>11</sub>–Cm<sub>7</sub>–D{{music|flat}}maj<sub>13</sub>–E{{music|flat}}<sub>9sus</sub>. Usher's voice spans from the low note of E{{music|flat}}<sub>4</sub> to the high note of A{{music|flat}}<sub>5</sub>.<ref name="sheet">{{cite web|url=http://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtdVPE.asp?ppn=MN0041201 |title=Usher - Nice & Slow Sheet Music |publisher=Musicnotes.com [[Universal Music Publishing Group]] |access-date=March 28, 2011}}</ref> "Nice & Slow" features a spoken introduction,<ref name="sheet"/> while in the middle of the song Usher performs a melodic [[rapping|rap]],<ref name="MyWay"/> which ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]''{{'s}} Shawnee Smith compared to the style of [[Do or Die (group)|Do or Die]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2gkEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA20 |title=LaFace Goes Back to School for Usher's Sophomore Set |first=Shawnee |last=Smith |location=New York |page=20 |date=August 16, 1997 |volume=109 |issue=33 |magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |publisher=[[Nielsen Business Media]] |issn=0006-2510}}</ref> Usher said to ''[[Time (magazine)|Time]]'' that "Nice & Slow" is "somewhat of an intimate story between a man and a woman."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,987859,00.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110129153709/http://www.time.com/time/magazine/article/0,9171,987859,00.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 29, 2011 |title=People: Feb. 23, 1998 |first=Joel |last=Stein |date=February 23, 1998 |access-date=March 28, 2011}}</ref>
sections.text:
"Nice & Slow" was written by Usher, Jermaine Dupri, Manuel Seal, and Brian Casey, with Dupri producing the tune and Seal serving as co-producer and responsible for the guitar work. Jagged Edge provided background vocals in the record. "Nice & Slow" was recorded by Phil Tan at the Somewhere in College Park studio in College Park, Georgia. Tan and Dupri mixed the record with assistance from John and Brian Frye at Studio LaCoCo, in Atlanta, Georgia. Dupri recalled telling Usher he needed a ballad to "knock out the world". The beat was created first, and the lyrics were fitted to it. The composition and recording of "Nice & Slow" took four hours, according to Dupri.

"Nice & Slow" is a slow R&B and soul ballad with hip hop influences. Musicologist Richard J. Ripani wrote that "Nice & Slow" is an example of the typical "R&B ballad style that became widely popular" in the late 1990s. According to the sheet music published at Musicnotes.com by Universal Music Publishing Group, "Nice & Slow" is written in common time with a slow tempo of sixty-eight beats per minute. Set in the key of A{{music|flat}} major, it follows the basic chord progression of Fm<sub>11</sub>–Cm<sub>7</sub>–D{{music|flat}}maj<sub>13</sub>–E{{music|flat}}<sub>9sus</sub>. Usher's voice spans from the low note of E{{music|flat}}<sub>4</sub> to the high note of A{{music|flat}}<sub>5</sub>. "Nice & Slow" features a spoken introduction, while in the middle of the song Usher performs a melodic rap, which Billboard{{'s}} Shawnee Smith compared to the style of Do or Die. Usher said to Time that "Nice & Slow" is "somewhat of an intimate story between a man and a woman."

sections.heading: Release
sections.wikitext: "Nice & Slow" was released via [[CD single]] and [[cassette single]] in the United States on January 6, 1998.<ref name="usrel">{{cite web|url=https://wemissmusic.com/2021/01/06/anniversary-of-ushers-nice-slow/|title=23rd Anniversary of Usher's 'Nice & Slow'|publisher=We Miss Music|date=January 6, 2021|access-date=October 27, 2021}}</ref><ref name="CDS"/><ref name="CAS"/> On February 3, 1998, it was serviced to US [[contemporary hit radio]].<ref>{{cite magazine|title=New Releases|magazine=[[Radio & Records]]|issue=1233|page=53|date=January 30, 1998}}</ref> A [[maxi single]] was released on March 2, 1998, and a remixes CD was made available on March 9, 1998.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.de/Nice-Slow-Usher/dp/B0000087WH/ref=sr_1_3?s=music&ie=UTF8&qid=1301298146&sr=1-3 |title=Nice & Slow |publisher=[[Amazon.de]] |access-date=March 28, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/Nice-Slow-Remixes-Usher/dp/B0000087WH/ref=tmm_acd_title_3 |title=Nice & Slow: The Remixes |website=Amazon |access-date=March 28, 2011}}</ref> In the United Kingdom, "Nice & Slow" was issued as CD single, a [[12-inch single]], and a cassette single on April 20, 1998.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=New Releases: Singles|magazine=[[Music Week]]|page=27|date=April 18, 1998}}</ref>
sections.text: "Nice & Slow" was released via CD single and cassette single in the United States on January 6, 1998. On February 3, 1998, it was serviced to US contemporary hit radio. A maxi single was released on March 2, 1998, and a remixes CD was made available on March 9, 1998. In the United Kingdom, "Nice & Slow" was issued as CD single, a 12-inch single, and a cassette single on April 20, 1998.

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: A writer for the ''[[Daily News (New York)|Daily News]]'' complimented the song as "warmly engaging".<ref name="check">{{cite web|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-83943339.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105171045/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-83943339.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=November 5, 2012 |title=Sound Check (L.A. Life) |date=October 3, 1997 |work=[[Daily News (New York)|Daily News]] |via=[[HighBeam Research]] |url-access=subscription |location=Los Angeles, CA |access-date=March 4, 2011}}</ref> A writer for [[Jet (magazine)|Jet]] praised Usher's "tender" vocals on the "sensuous ballad", stating that he displayed romance on the song.<ref name="romance">{{cite journal|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RDsDAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA61 |title=Hot Male Singers Keep Romance Alive |page=61 |date=September 14, 1998 |journal=[[Jet (magazine)|Jet]] |publisher=[[Johnson Publishing Company]] |issn=0021-5996 |volume=94 |issue=16}}</ref> British magazine ''[[Music Week]]'' wrote, "More ultra-smooth R&B from the crown prince of hip-hop soul, "Nice & Slow" is a superbly mellow, seductive tune which has Usher showing off his unhurried rapping skills."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=|last=|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1998/Music-Week-1998-04-11.pdf|title=Single reviews|work=[[Music Week]]|date=April 11, 1998|page=24|access-date=September 15, 2023}}</ref> In 2016, ''[[Complex Networks|Complex]]'' ranked the song number seven on their list of the 25 greatest Usher songs,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.complex.com/music/best-usher-songs/|title=The 25 Best Usher Songs|website=[[Complex Networks|Complex]]|date=October 14, 2016|accessdate=March 29, 2022}}</ref> and in 2021, ''[[American Songwriter]]'' ranked the song number eight on their list of the 10 greatest Usher songs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://americansongwriter.com/top-10-usher-songs/|title=Top 10 Usher Songs|first=Jacob|last=Uitti|website=[[American Songwriter]]|date=December 18, 2021|accessdate=March 29, 2022}}</ref>
sections.text: A writer for the Daily News complimented the song as "warmly engaging". A writer for Jet praised Usher's "tender" vocals on the "sensuous ballad", stating that he displayed romance on the song. British magazine Music Week wrote, "More ultra-smooth R&B from the crown prince of hip-hop soul, "Nice & Slow" is a superbly mellow, seductive tune which has Usher showing off his unhurried rapping skills." In 2016, Complex ranked the song number seven on their list of the 25 greatest Usher songs, and in 2021, American Songwriter ranked the song number eight on their list of the 10 greatest Usher songs.

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: "Nice & Slow" debuted at number nine on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] on the chart dated January 24, 1998, as "[[You Make Me Wanna...]]", the first single from ''My Way'' slipped from number seven to number ten.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/#/charts/hot-100?chartDate=1998-01-24&order=position |title=Hot 100 |magazine=Billboard |publisher=Nielsen Business Media |date=January 24, 2011 |access-date=April 6, 2011}}</ref> On February 2, 1998, the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA) awarded the song a [[RIAA certification|gold certification]], following up with a platinum one on February 12.<ref name="RIAAcert"/> "Nice & Slow" continued to ascend the Hot 100, reaching number one on February 14, succeeding "[[Together Again (Janet Jackson song)|Together Again]]" by [[Janet Jackson]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/#/charts/hot-100?chartDate=1998-02-14 |title=Hot 100 |magazine=Billboard |publisher=Nielsen Business Media |date=February 14, 2011 |access-date=April 6, 2011}}</ref> It remained atop the chart on February 21, but on February 28 it was replaced by [[Celine Dion]]'s "[[My Heart Will Go On]]".<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/#/charts/hot-100?chartDate=1998-02-28 |title=Hot 100 |magazine=Billboard |publisher=Nielsen Business Media |date=February 28, 2011 |access-date=April 6, 2011}}</ref> On the [[UK Singles Chart]], "Nice & Slow" reached number 24.<ref name="TOCC"/>
sections.text: "Nice & Slow" debuted at number nine on the Billboard Hot 100 on the chart dated January 24, 1998, as "You Make Me Wanna...", the first single from My Way slipped from number seven to number ten. On February 2, 1998, the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA) awarded the song a gold certification, following up with a platinum one on February 12. "Nice & Slow" continued to ascend the Hot 100, reaching number one on February 14, succeeding "Together Again" by Janet Jackson. It remained atop the chart on February 21, but on February 28 it was replaced by Celine Dion's "My Heart Will Go On". On the UK Singles Chart, "Nice & Slow" reached number 24.

sections.wikitext: The music video for the song was directed by [[Hype Williams]] and shot in [[Paris]] in February 1998.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CywEAAAAMBAJ&pg=PA87 |title=Super man child |first=Andréa |last=Duncan |journal=[[Vibe (magazine)|Vibe]] |publisher=[[InterMedia Partners]] |page=87 |date=February 1998 |volume=6 |issue=1 |issn=1070-4701}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mtv.com/videos/usher/157935/nice-slow.jhtml |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081030030742/http://www.mtv.com/videos/usher/157935/nice-slow.jhtml |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 30, 2008 |title=Usher " Music Videos |publisher=MTV |date=February 11, 1998 |access-date=March 28, 2011}}</ref> [[Kimora Lee Simmons]] plays Usher's love interest.<ref name="Q102">{{cite web|url=http://q104.radio.com/2011/01/26/video-rewind-usher-nice-and-slow/ |title=Video Rewind: Usher – 'Nice And Slow' |first=Erin |last=Fox |publisher=[[WQAL]]. [[CBS Radio]] |date=January 26, 2011 |access-date=April 15, 2011}}</ref> The video opens with the caption "4:00 pm Paris" as Usher gets out of an airplane. He is shown shirtless in a hotel room having a telephone conversation with his love interest, consisting of the song's spoken intro. Usher and Simmons prepare for their date and meet each other before sightseeing around Paris in a [[convertible (car)|convertible]]. Interspersed are [[low-angle shot]]s of Usher dancing on a sidewalk. As the day becomes night, Usher is seen wearing sunglasses playing the guitar and dancing shirtless in front of the [[Eiffel Tower]].<ref name="Q102"/> Usher and Simmons drive across a bridge, and midway they are confronted by several [[gangster]]s, who kidnap and cage Simmons and beat Usher.<ref name="Q102"/> Usher appeals to the police, who are apparently of no help, and proceeds to locate the gangsters' lair himself. He offers a briefcase to the gangsters, which explodes after being opened and a grenade starts to blow. Usher and the gangsters then engage in [[hand-to-hand combat]]. Usher and Simmons are together riding escape away on a motorbike as the windows of the building behind them explode. They are then seen relaxing on a sofa in triumphant before she saw a computer zoomed in, which features the song's title written over and over on a word processor. The music video on [[YouTube]] has received over 80 million views as of May 2024.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DIpQ4AZSAf8 Usher - Nice & Slow (Official HD Video)].[[YouTube]]</ref>
sections.text: The music video for the song was directed by Hype Williams and shot in Paris in February 1998. Kimora Lee Simmons plays Usher's love interest. The video opens with the caption "4:00 pm Paris" as Usher gets out of an airplane. He is shown shirtless in a hotel room having a telephone conversation with his love interest, consisting of the song's spoken intro. Usher and Simmons prepare for their date and meet each other before sightseeing around Paris in a convertible. Interspersed are low-angle shots of Usher dancing on a sidewalk. As the day becomes night, Usher is seen wearing sunglasses playing the guitar and dancing shirtless in front of the Eiffel Tower. Usher and Simmons drive across a bridge, and midway they are confronted by several gangsters, who kidnap and cage Simmons and beat Usher. Usher appeals to the police, who are apparently of no help, and proceeds to locate the gangsters' lair himself. He offers a briefcase to the gangsters, which explodes after being opened and a grenade starts to blow. Usher and the gangsters then engage in hand-to-hand combat. Usher and Simmons are together riding escape away on a motorbike as the windows of the building behind them explode. They are then seen relaxing on a sofa in triumphant before she saw a computer zoomed in, which features the song's title written over and over on a word processor. The music video on YouTube has received over 80 million views as of May 2024.
